questions.q:
Consider the following statements about tropical evergreen forests in India:
1. They occur in regions receiving very heavy rainfall, generally above 200 cm.
2. All trees shed their leaves together in one dry season.
3. They are found in the Western Ghats, parts of Assam and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Heavy, well-distributed rain and a short dry spell keep these forests green, so there is no single leaf-fall season; trees shed leaves at different times. Hence statement 2 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Ch 15

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT an adaptation of mangrove plants to their waterlogged, saline habitat?
o: Pneumatophores that rise above the mud
Stilt roots that anchor the plant in soft mud
Viviparous germination of seeds on the parent plant
Deep tap roots reaching the freshwater table
questions.e: Mangrove soil is soft, saline and oxygen-poor, so plants grow shallow, spreading roots with aerial breathing roots rather than deep tap roots. Pneumatophores, stilt roots and vivipary are classic adaptations.

questions.q: As per the India State of Forest Report series, which State has the largest mangrove cover in India?
questions.e: The Indian Sundarbans in West Bengal form the biggest mangrove block in India. Gujarat comes second, mainly because of Kachchh and the Gulf coast.

questions.q:
Consider the following wetlands:
1. Chilika Lake
2. Keoladeo National Park
3. Loktak Lake
Which of the above are currently listed in the Montreux Record?
questions.e: The Montreux Record lists Ramsar sites where ecological character has changed or is likely to change. Keoladeo and Loktak are on it; Chilika was removed in 2002 after restoration of its mouth and salinity.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the forest types of India:
1. Tropical moist deciduous forests are the most widespread forest type in India.
2. Teak and sal are characteristic species of moist deciduous forests.
3. Moist deciduous forests receive roughly 100 to 200 cm of rainfall.
4. Tropical dry deciduous forests receive more than 200 cm of rainfall.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Dry deciduous forests grow in the 70-100 cm belt; more than 200 cm belongs to evergreen forests. Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Ch 15

questions.q:
Statement-I: Reef-building corals are found mainly in warm, shallow and clear tropical waters.
Statement-II: Corals live in symbiosis with zooxanthellae algae that need sunlight for photosynthesis.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Zooxanthellae supply food to the coral polyp and need light, so reefs are confined to shallow, sunlit, clear and warm water. Statement-II is the direct cause behind Statement-I.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about coral bleaching:
1. It occurs when corals expel their symbiotic zooxanthellae under stress.
2. A bleached coral is always dead at once.
3. A rise in sea surface temperature can trigger it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Corals lose colour and their main food source when zooxanthellae leave, and heat stress is a main trigger. Bleached corals can recover if conditions normalise soon, so they are not always dead.
questions.h: Hot water, algae out, coral turns white

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a major coral reef area of India?
questions.e: India's reefs are in the Gulf of Mannar, Gulf of Kachchh, Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The Sundarbans is a muddy, turbid mangrove delta where reefs cannot grow.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of lakes and the States in which they are located:
1. Loktak : Manipur
2. Sambhar : Rajasthan
3. Pulicat : Karnataka
4. Wular : Himachal Pradesh
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Loktak is in Manipur and Sambhar in Rajasthan. Pulicat straddles Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, and Wular is in Jammu and Kashmir.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of rivers drain into the sea through estuaries rather than deltas?
questions.e: The Narmada and Tapi flow west through rift valleys in a straight course, and strong tides plus little silt prevent delta building. East-flowing peninsular rivers and the Ganga-Brahmaputra make deltas.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Ch 3

questions.q:
Statement-I: Mangroves reduce the damage caused by storm surges and cyclones on tropical coasts.
Statement-II: Mangroves grow only in freshwater swamps far inland.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Dense stilt roots and trunks dissipate wave energy, so Statement-I is correct. Mangroves are salt-tolerant plants of tidal coasts and estuaries, not inland freshwater swamps.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the tundra biome:
1. Arctic tundra is underlain by permafrost.
2. Lichens, mosses and dwarf shrubs are typical vegetation.
3. Alpine tundra occurs only in polar latitudes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Alpine tundra occurs above the tree line on high mountains, including at low latitudes, so 'only in polar latitudes' is wrong. Permafrost and a low-growing lichen-moss-shrub cover mark the Arctic tundra.
questions.h: Tundra: tiny plants on frozen floor

questions.q: The boreal coniferous forest (taiga) belt is characterised by which of the following?
o: Needle-shaped leaves and conical tree crowns that shed snow
Scattered trees in a continuous grass cover
Dense epiphytes and lianas in several tree layers
questions.e: Conical shape and needle leaves let heavy snow slide off and reduce water loss in cold, physiologically dry conditions. Epiphytes and lianas mark rainforests, and scattered trees in grass mark savanna.

questions.q:
Match the grassland with the region where it is found:
A. Prairies
B. Pampas
C. Veld
D. Downs
1. Australia
2. South Africa
3. Argentina and Uruguay
4. North America
questions.e: Prairies are North American, pampas lie in Argentina and Uruguay, the veld is in South Africa and the downs are in Australia. Steppes are the Eurasian equivalent.
questions.s: Majid Husain / NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography

questions.q: Savanna ecosystems differ from temperate grasslands in that savannas:
o: lack any tree cover and occur in cool, mid-latitude interiors
have scattered trees and a pronounced wet and dry season in the tropics
are covered by dense evergreen trees with no dry season
questions.e: Savannas are tropical grasslands with scattered trees and a distinct dry season, often shaped by fire and grazing animals. Temperate grasslands like steppes and prairies have cold winters and almost no trees.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 14 (Biodiversity)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about deserts:
1. The Atacama Desert is made arid partly by the cold Humboldt (Peru) current.
2. The Gobi is a cold desert.
3. Ladakh is a hot desert of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Cold current air is stable and carries little moisture, so the Atacama coast gets almost no rain; the Gobi has very cold winters. Ladakh is a high-altitude cold desert, not a hot one.
questions.s: Majid Husain, World Geography; Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q: Which of the following is a cold desert in India?
questions.e: Spiti and Ladakh lie in the rain shadow of the Himalaya at high altitude, giving cold, dry conditions. Thar and the Rann are hot, low-lying arid or salt-marsh regions.

questions.q: Plants such as cacti follow Crassulacean Acid Metabolism (CAM). How does this help them in deserts?
o: They open stomata during midday for faster gas exchange
They store carbon only in deep tap roots
They fix atmospheric nitrogen through root nodules
They open stomata at night to take in CO2 and so lose less water
questions.e: Night air is cooler and more humid, so water loss through open stomata is far less. CO2 is stored as organic acids and used in photosynthesis next day with stomata closed.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Biomes / NCERT Class XI Biology

questions.q: The kangaroo rat of North American deserts survives without drinking water mainly because it:
o: stores water in its stomach like a camel
feeds on succulent plants throughout the year
obtains water from the metabolic oxidation of dry seeds and concentrates its urine
drinks dew collected on fur every morning
questions.e: Oxidation of food produces metabolic water, and highly concentrated urine reduces loss. This is a standard example of physiological adaptation to arid zones.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Ch 13 (Organisms and Populations)

questions.q: The Desert National Park near Jaisalmer is best known for the protection of which species?
questions.e: The park in the Thar desert shelters the critically endangered Great Indian Bustard, a ground-nesting bird of arid grasslands. The other animals live in the Himalaya, Kashmir valley and Brahmaputra floodplains.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Little Rann of Kutch is correct?
o: It is a freshwater swamp in the Brahmaputra valley
It is a saline desert wetland that is the last refuge of the Indian wild ass
It is a coastal mangrove sanctuary in Odisha
It is a high-altitude cold desert in Ladakh
questions.e: The Little Rann of Kutch in Gujarat is a seasonally flooded salt marsh that supports the Indian wild ass (Khur). It is unrelated to Odisha mangroves or Ladakh.

questions.q: The Shola forests, a mix of stunted evergreen forest and grassland patches, are found in:
o: the Terai belt of the Himalayan foothills
the high hills of the southern Western Ghats such as the Nilgiris and Anamalais
questions.e: Sholas are southern montane wet temperate forests in sheltered folds of hills with grassland on exposed slopes. Terai has tall grasslands and moist forest, not montane Sholas.

questions.q: The Banni grassland, noted as one of the largest grassland tracts of Asia, lies in:
questions.e: Banni lies on the edge of the Great Rann of Kachchh, with saline soil and seasonal flooding. It supports cattle-rearing pastoralists such as the Maldharis.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Terai grasslands of India:
1. They lie along the foothills of the Himalaya.
2. They support species such as the one-horned rhinoceros and swamp deer.
3. They are typical of the arid interior of Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Terai is a high-rainfall, marshy belt of tall grass and forest at the Himalayan foot. Arid Rajasthan has desert scrub and short grass, not Terai.

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes the temperate deciduous forest biome?
o: Broad-leaved trees that shed leaves in autumn in regions with four distinct seasons
Stunted shrubs in winter-rain Mediterranean climate only
questions.e: Shedding leaves before winter reduces water loss and frost damage. Oak, maple and beech are typical trees.

questions.q: The Ramsar Convention on Wetlands was adopted in 1971 in a city of which country, and is observed through World Wetlands Day on which date?
questions.e: The treaty was signed at Ramsar on the Caspian Sea in Iran on 2 February 1971, which is why World Wetlands Day falls on 2 February. 22 March is World Water Day.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Loktak Lake:
1. It is the largest freshwater lake in north-east India.
2. Phumdis are floating masses of vegetation, soil and organic matter in it.
3. Keibul Lamjao National Park, the only floating national park in the world, lies within it.
4. It is located in Nagaland.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Loktak lies in Manipur, not Nagaland. The phumdis support Keibul Lamjao National Park, the home of the Sangai (brow-antlered deer).

questions.q:
Match the Ramsar site with its State:
A. Harike
B. Kolleru
C. Deepor Beel
D. Ashtamudi
1. Kerala
2. Assam
3. Andhra Pradesh
4. Punjab
questions.e: Harike (Punjab) is at the Beas-Sutlej confluence, Kolleru lies between the Godavari and Krishna deltas, Deepor Beel is near Guwahati and Ashtamudi is a Kerala backwater.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Pulicat Lake:
1. It is the second largest brackish water lagoon in India after Chilika.
2. Sriharikota island separates it from the Bay of Bengal.
3. It lies entirely within Odisha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Pulicat spans Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, with the Sriharikota barrier island on its seaward side. Chilika in Odisha is the largest.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a meteor-impact crater lake in basalt rock that is saline and alkaline?
questions.e: Lonar in Maharashtra formed from a meteorite impact in the Deccan basalt. Sambhar is a Rajasthan salt lake and Dal is a Kashmir freshwater lake.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Excess nutrient input from fertilisers and sewage can cause a lake to lose dissolved oxygen.
Statement-II: Nutrient enrichment causes algal blooms whose decomposition consumes oxygen.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: This is eutrophication: algae bloom, die and are decomposed by bacteria that use up oxygen, raising BOD and harming fish. Statement-II explains Statement-I.

questions.q: In a lake, the zone of shallow water near the shore where rooted plants grow is called the:
questions.e: Light reaches the bottom in the littoral zone so rooted plants thrive. The limnetic zone is open sunlit water and the profundal zone is deep, light-poor water.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology / Shankar IAS

questions.q: Which of the following statements about estuaries is correct?
o: They are formed only in the interior of continents
They are partially enclosed coastal areas where fresh river water mixes with sea water and salinity varies with tides
They are always free of tidal influence
They always have a constant salinity equal to sea water
questions.e: Tidal mixing makes salinity fluctuate, and nutrient-rich sediments make estuaries highly productive nurseries for fish and shellfish.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sundarbans:
1. The Sundari tree (Heritiera fomes) gives the region its name.
2. It lies in the delta of the Ganga, Brahmaputra and Meghna rivers.
3. It is the largest mangrove forest in India but not in the world.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Sundarbans, shared with Bangladesh, is the world's largest contiguous mangrove forest, so statement 3 is wrong. Sundari is a dominant species.

questions.q: Bhitarkanika mangroves in Odisha are best known for:
o: Saltwater crocodiles and the Gahirmatha olive ridley nesting beach nearby
questions.e: Bhitarkanika, in the Brahmani-Baitarani delta, is the second major mangrove ecosystem of India after the Sundarbans. Dugongs are found in the Gulf of Mannar and Andaman waters.

questions.q: Which was the first Marine National Park of India, set up in 1982?
o: Marine National Park in the Gulf of Kachchh, Gujarat
Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park
questions.e: The Gulf of Kachchh marine park near Jamnagar was India's first, protecting corals and mangroves. Gulf of Mannar and Wandoor were declared later.

questions.q: The Gulf of Mannar was designated as India's first Marine Biosphere Reserve. It is in the State of:
questions.e: The Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve lies off the Tamil Nadu coast and is known for corals, seagrass and the dugong. It was notified in 1989.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about coral reefs:
1. Fringing reefs grow directly attached to the shore.
2. Atolls are ring-shaped reefs enclosing a lagoon.
3. Lakshadweep consists mostly of coral atolls.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Darwin's classification recognises fringing, barrier and atoll reefs. Lakshadweep islands are coral formations on submerged ridges, mostly atolls.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the largest coral reef system in the world?
questions.e: The Great Barrier Reef off Queensland, Australia, is the largest living structure on earth by size. The Mesoamerican Reef is the largest in the Atlantic-Caribbean region.

questions.q: Coral polyps build their hard skeleton chiefly from which compound?
questions.e: Corals extract calcium and carbonate ions from seawater. Ocean acidification lowers carbonate availability and so threatens skeleton formation.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct about hydrothermal vent communities in the deep sea?
o: They are limited to shallow coral lagoons
They depend on photosynthesis by phytoplankton above them
Primary production is done by chemosynthetic bacteria
They occur only in the photic zone
questions.e: Bacteria oxidise hydrogen sulphide from vents to make food, supporting tube worms and other animals in total darkness.

questions.q: Upwelling zones such as those off Peru are rich fishing grounds because:
o: warm surface water sinks to the bottom
rivers deposit large amounts of silt
cold, nutrient-rich deep water rises to the sunlit surface
questions.e: Nutrients raise phytoplankton production, which supports the food chain up to fish like anchovy. Peru's Humboldt current is a classic case.

questions.q: The zone of the ocean where light is sufficient for photosynthesis is called the:
questions.e: It extends roughly to 200 m in clear open ocean. Below it lies the dark aphotic zone.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Estuaries act as nurseries for many commercially important fish and prawn species.
Statement-II: Estuaries have abundant nutrients and sheltered, low-salinity water that protects juveniles.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Nutrients carried by rivers and trapped by tides plus shelter from predators make estuaries ideal nurseries. Statement-II explains Statement-I.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about wetlands:
1. Under the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017, paddy fields are not treated as wetlands.
2. The Ramsar Convention requires members to promote the wise use of all wetlands.
3. Designation as a Ramsar site automatically makes the area a protected area under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Ramsar designation is not itself a legal protection and does not automatically bring a site under the Wildlife Act; India regulates wetlands through its own laws and rules. Paddy fields and river channels are excluded from the 2017 Rules.

questions.q: Sambhar Lake is best described as:
o: the largest inland saline lake in India, in Rajasthan
questions.e: Sambhar is a shallow saline lake that supplies salt and attracts flamingos in winter. It is a Ramsar site.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of habitat and typical organism is NOT correctly matched?
questions.e: Kelp needs sunlight and cool shallow water, while vent communities live in darkness on chemosynthesis. The other three pairs are standard associations.

questions.q: Tso Moriri, a Ramsar site, is a high-altitude lake in:
questions.e: Tso Moriri in Changthang, Ladakh, is a brackish high-altitude lake that is a breeding ground for the black-necked crane.

questions.q: Seagrass meadows are ecologically important because they:
o: grow in the deep aphotic zone
are a type of seaweed with no roots or flowers
are the only plants that fix nitrogen in the ocean
stabilise sediments, store carbon and feed species like dugongs
questions.e: Seagrasses are flowering plants rooted in shallow seabeds. They are blue carbon sinks and the main food of dugongs.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about mangrove ecosystems:
1. They act as nurseries for fish and prawns.
2. They help trap sediments and prevent coastal erosion.
3. They are found in the cold temperate coasts of Europe.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Mangroves are tropical and subtropical tidal forests, so cold temperate Europe does not have them. Their root tangle slows water, traps silt and shelters juvenile fish.
